handback.t:
K5 result: the success criterion is NOT met by any arm in either text world, and the control deficit is the front router, not the retrieval layer. Everything is synthetic outcomes on real text (h13 fixtures), no real traffic, no src edits, no commits, no downloads.

The criterion was Holm wins vs best fair in T12 / T12-drift / T48 and no Holm loss (or TOST ±.01) in ctl-irrel / ctl-oneoff / ctl-noinfo, in A and B. Only the confirm runs carry a verdict.

**Verdict (frozen picks, confirm A 61-90 | B 61-90, H2000 vs best fair BF7, which now includes global-ts)**
- **Same front:** retrieval is harmless to positive in the controls. g1|meta3 minus the same meta-front without retrieval: ctl-irrel -.003|-.001, ctl-oneoff +.020*|+.013, ctl-noinfo +.009|+.002. In the dependent worlds it adds +.035*|+.026 (T12), +.037*|+.025 (drift), +.016*|+.010 (T48).
- **Controls vs global-ts:** with topic-keyed fronts the controls fail because global-ts is the best fair baseline there. g1|warm is -.053!|-.060! (ctl-irrel) and -.036!|-.032! (ctl-noinfo). It sits above the old 6-baseline best fair (BF6, without global-ts) by +.09|+.08 and +.024.
- **g1|warm vs BF6:** it passes A confirm outright (3/3 wins, 0 control losses). It misses only T48 in B (+.003 n.s.).
- **Pipeline-level Thompson meta** over {warm+retrieval, global-ts}, tuned on seeds 1-8:
  - P2w+ gets ctl-irrel -.004e|-.003e (TOST-equivalent in both worlds).
  - ctl-oneoff is +.011|+.015*.
  - ctl-noinfo is -.012!|-.011 (the small-gap case).
  - T12 +.023*|+.017*, drift +.027*|+.022*, T48 -.006|-.002.
  - No variant wins T48.
- **Price of online front selection** vs the oracle front per world is about -.004 to -.02 in every world.
- **Cause:** bandit regret on Bernoulli rewards with gaps of .03-.12. My argument that no cleverer off-policy estimator avoids it (deterministic keyed choice) is not separately tested.
- **Gates on the vote** (g16 safe/shrinkage, anchor-local Bayes test with asymmetric-loss threshold, online A/B holdout) do not help.
  - They keep roughly 15-40% of the ungated gain in dependent worlds. Example, A confirm T12 vs the meta-front without retrieval: g1 +.035*, safe +.006, shrink +.009, local +.008, A/B +.014.
  - They do not fix the controls: shrink|meta3 is -.020!, -.013!, -.018! in A confirm.
  - The A/B holdout withholds the layer on about 50% of T12 tasks and flaps; the effect is too small to resolve in 2000 tasks.
  - h13's "ungated layer needs no gate" is confirmed, including on the new control ctl-noinfo.
- **Cold start:** the pipeline meta recovers about 80% of global-ts's early lead in ctl-irrel by task 250 (H250). In T12 it ties guarded.

**Post-hoc, no verdict:** ablation arms were appended after the confirm, so they need a fresh-seed frozen run before any claim.
- **Anchor feature only:** `feat|warm`, with the retrieved anchor injected as a plain feature into warm(hebr), no vote, no gate, no context, was the strongest arm.
  - T12 +.042*|+.034*, drift +.041*|+.033*, ctl-oneoff +.025*|+.030*, T48 +.017*|+.011 (n.s. in B).
  - It still loses to global-ts in ctl-irrel (-.058!|-.059!) and ctl-noinfo (-.038!|-.032!).
- **Context injection:** the real top-1 paragraph has precision .12-.35, below the ~.57 break-even of the assumed 15%-gain / 5%-distraction model. The retrieval gain is routing, not context. That is a consequence of the assumed constants, not a measurement.

**Disclosed deviations**
- The A held-out split 31-60 is not clean. I looked at it in v1, and again in v2 after adding the pipeline-meta arms. The injection gate, the retrieval-parameter tuning for the warm pipeline and the 10-arm primary family were added after the v2 look.
- ctl-noinfo is a new control I defined before running any policy.
- global-ts is now in the fair set.
- Holm is computed inside a declared 10-arm primary family. Primary levels are bit-identical across reruns.
- Seeds 61-90 on A and B are consumed. No fresh seeds exist in the fixtures for any further iteration.
